newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Horn to speak at German Unity Day.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Horn to speak at German Unity Day.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn, credited with opening the way to the fall of the Berlin Wall, will address the main commemorations of German Unity Day in Munich on October 3, Hungary's foreign ministry said.

Horn has been invited to address a ceremony marking the anniversary of the unification of East and West Germany in 1990 by Bavarian Prime Minister Edmund Stoiber, who is also speaker-in-office of the upper house of the German Parliament.

The address will coincide with a two-day visit by Horn to Bavaria and Baden-Wurttemberg to promote investment in Hungary and to sign a delayed 500 million mark ($330 million) credit agreement between Hungary and the two German states.

As foreign minister in Hungary's last communist government, Horn gave the go-ahead in September 1989 to open Hungary's western border with Austria to tens of thousands of refugees from East Germany trying to reach the West.
Weeks later the Communist regime of East Germany collapsed and the Berlin Wall, which had divided the city for 28 years, was opened. The two Germanies eventually united on October 3, 1990.
